newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SMH sees sales more than doubling in 10 yrs.
newsitem.headline: SMH sees sales more than doubling in 10 yrs.

text.p: Swiss watchmaker Ste Suisse Microelectronique et d'Horologerie SA (SMH) believes the potential exists for group sales to more than double within the next 10 years.

"SMH should be able to produce gross turnover of between eight and 10 billion Swiss francs ($5.5 and $6.9 billion) within the next 10 years," SMH chairman Nicolas Hayek said in an interview with Reuters Financial Television.
He also said the company expected 1997 to be another good year for earnings growth.
"We expect 1997 to be a good year provided we do not have any problems with currencies," he added.
Hayek also said group sales for January 1997 were the highest ever reported for the month of January.
"It looks as if February is going to be a good month also," he said.

SMH on Tuesday reported that the group's net profit rose to 282 million Swiss francs in 1996 from 273 million francs in 1995. Sales were up to 2.789 billion from 2.637 billion. Cash flow rose to 462 million from 430 million.
SMH also raised its dividend to 18 percent from the 17 percent paid on 1995 results.
"The 1996 profit could have been higher, but we invested in new SMH distribution companies, especially in the Far East," Hayek said.
In the lower watch market segment, exchange rate-related losses have been for the most part offset by the recent decline of the Swiss franc on foreign exchange markets, Hayek said.

He said the goal for the company was to hold its position as the world's largest watchmaker and to increase turnover of watches and components to some 4.5 billion to 5.0 billion francs within the next six to eight years.

SMH, which a large and growing cash pile on hand, is watching out for the possibility of acquisitions, but the company's preferred method of expansion is through the development of new products, he also said.

"We have many alternatives...we are not a company that buys another company just to buy it and to please analysts for a short time. We will only take a company that fits into the culture and into the production and marketing approach," Hayek said.
SMH, with a world market share of between 20 and 22 percent, would only look to eventually buy one of the top makers in the watch industry, he added.

"There are no watch companies that we are looking to buy except one of the very best names if one would be free to sell in the near future...so what we're doing is investing in new products," he added.
Commenting on the company's joint venture with Mercedes Benz AG to build a two-seat city car, Hayek said he expected to so-called "Smart Car" to come to market in early 1998 as planned.
He said hoped the joint venture would reach its goal of producing 200,000 cars annually by 1999 or, as planned, by the year 2000.
SMH has a long-term target for car-related revenues of between two billion and three billion francs, he added.
In addition, Hayek said the company's activities in the telephone sector are moving ahead well.

SMH is targeting a goal for turnover of between one and two billion francs in the telecommunications sector within the next six to eight years. -- Zurich Editorial +41 1 631 7340 ($ = 1.459 Swiss Francs)
